To compute the dynamic pressure (q) in pascals, we use the formula:

\[ q = \frac{1}{2} \rho v^2 \]

where:
- \( \rho \) is the air density (0.4135 kg/m³),
- \( v \) is the speed in meters per second (m/s).

First, convert the speed from km/h to m/s:

\[ 900 \text{ km/h} = 900 \times \frac{1000 \text{ m}}{3600 \text{ s}} = 250 \text{ m/s} \]

Now plug the values into the formula:

\[ q = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.4135 \, \text{kg/m}^3 \times (250 \, \text{m/s})^2 \]

\[ q = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.4135 \times 62500 \]

\[ q = 0.20675 \times 62500 \]

\[ q = 12918.75 \, \text{Pa} \]

So, the dynamic pressure is **12918.75 Pa**.
